record.context_brief: small-threshold improvement of a topological degree estimate
record.original_question: For a continuous map f: S^1 -> S^1 and delta > 0, define I_delta(f) as the double integral over pairs (x,y) in S^1 x S^1 with |f(x)-f(y)| >= delta of dx dy / |x-y|^2. Does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f| <= c delta I_delta(f) for every continuous f: S^1 -> S^1 and every delta <= sqrt(3)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.3 ([17, Open Problem 3]). Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that |deg f| <= c delta I_delta(f) for all f in C(S^1;S^1) and all delta <= sqrt(3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle, equipped with arc-length measure. For a continuous map $f:S^1\to S^1$, let $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ denote its topological degree. For each $\delta>0$, define
$$ I_\delta(f) \;=\; \iint_{\{(x,y)\in S^1\times S^1\,:\,|f(x)-f(y)|\ge \delta\}} \frac{dx\,dy}{|x-y|^2}, $$
where $|x-y|$ denotes the Euclidean (chordal) distance in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$ such that
$$ |\deg f| \;\le\; c\,\delta\, I_\delta(f) $$
for every continuous map $f:S^1\to S^1$ and every $\delta\in(0,\sqrt{3}]$?
artifact.status_search_result: The estimate is known for sufficiently small $\delta$ (with constants depending on a small threshold), and the question whether it can be extended up to the threshold $\sqrt{3}$ was posed as an open problem by Brezis (and earlier by Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen). Web searches did not reveal a resolution of this small-threshold improvement; recent work on Bourgain–Brezis–Mironescu type formulas does not address this specific endpoint, so the status appears to remain open but could not be definitively confirmed.

status_evidence.title: Some of my favorite open problems (H. Brezis)
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 5.3: Does there exist a (universal) constant c such that |deg f| ≤ c δ I_δ(f) for all f ∈ C(S^1;S^1) and all δ ≤ √3?
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open problem with the explicit threshold √3.

status_evidence.title: Lifting, Degree, and Distributional Jacobian Revisited (Bourgain–Brezis–Mironescu)
status_evidence.snippet: Estimates for the topological degree of continuous maps from a sphere into itself using double integrals of the form I_δ.
status_evidence.claim: Source of the original degree estimate that the open problem seeks to sharpen.
